comment: Basically, if you have taken stats before, you will be fine. If this is your first time taking the course, you may struggle to learn the material.  He typically assigns Aplia homework and hand-in homework for every class. This is always on material he hasn't yet taught which is very confusing. All in all, wouldn't recommend for someone new to stats
Sit in front. Be pretty. Go to office hours.

He is a great professor. He is very clear in class, and very helpful during office hours. Tests are not hard at all, he doesn't try to trick or fail you. He also gives you a formula sheet, and for the second test a guide sheet - both are very helpful.

He's a really nice guy but overall he's an average teacher. Class can get boring at time. He tries to make sure that everyone understands. His tests are not really hard but they are tricky and might surprise you. If you are gonna take b-stats might as well be with him, even if he's not the best teacher.

I really liked this class. He uses real life examples for material that can be hard to grasp. I took stats in high school so I was a little familiar with the material but he explained the concepts really well. I even won five dollars by guessing the outcomes of college basketball games. Needless to say I would like to take another class by him.
The tools taught are useful, but the class is extremely boring. Take it only if you NEED knowledge in Econometrics for your career.
very boring and cannot explain it to you outside of class.  He will call on you to do problems when your hand isn't raised.  i wouln't take him again
Good professor, not too hard. Do the homework and ask questions in class, you'll do fine.

Meh. Not the worst, not the best. His lectures were pretty boring, and he ALWAYS let us out at least 5 minutes late. Tests were long and difficult. Make sure to keep on top of the material. Don't bother trying to meet with him outside of class- he'll just confuse you more if you didn't catch it the first time.

Good guy, knows his stuff, but didn't like how he waited til the last minute to give us the final project worth 25% of the grade.  This course was basically just like an advanced business statistics class without nearly enough emphasis on the economics component.  Also, class was boring at times and he was often difficult to meet with.

One of the nicest profs in Bschool but he is definitely a challenging prof. His tests are difficult and require you to apply what you've learned in class rather than just regurgitate it.  You have to pay attention to what he says in class to do well.  I ended up with a A-.
great guy and really friendly.  all you have to do is keep up with the homework and make sure you know what's going on, and it's really not difficult.  definitley reccommended.

Schmidt is tough, had him for bstat I.  Keep up with the hw or else forget it.  Tests are pretty hard, he likes being technical and trying to trip you up.  His own explanations are sometimes confusing and the book isn't much clearer.  Try to avoid him for bstat I, in class lectures are boring and will put you to sleep.

Professor Schmidt is a great professor even though he occasionally leaves new material for the last 30 minutes of class before an exam.  Nevertheless, he is very thorough and very helpful.  He tells you everything you need to know for the test without confusing you with useless details.
